title: State Machine From a Diagram
statement:
Implement the state machine this diagram describes.

## The diagram

```
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Draft
    Draft --> Review: submit
    Review --> Draft: reject
    Review --> Approved: approve
    Approved --> Draft: revise
    Approved --> Published: publish
    Published --> Archived: archive
    Archived --> [*]
```

*Guides → Diagram* (**F2**) draws it.

## Your function

```
enum doc_state { DRAFT, REVIEW, APPROVED, PUBLISHED, ARCHIVED };

int transition(int state, const char *event);
```

Return the state reached from `state` on `event`, or `-1` if the diagram has
no arrow for that pair.

The harness starts the document in `DRAFT`, feeds you one event per line, and
prints the state name after each -- or `REFUSED` when you return `-1`, leaving
the state where it was.

## Watch out

- Every pair the diagram does not draw is a refusal. There are five states and
  six events, so thirty combinations, and only six of them are arrows.
- `Archived` has no outgoing arrow. Once there, everything is refused.
- An event name that is not on the diagram at all -- `frobnicate` -- is
  refused like any other pair, not a crash.
- `event` is a C string, so `==` compares pointers. You want `strcmp`.
- A diagram is a table. Writing it as one -- an array of
  `{from, event, to}` rows -- gets you a function that is checkable against
  the picture line by line. A nest of `if` statements does the same job and
  cannot be read next to the diagram.

generator.source:
"""Random event sequences for the review workflow.

The alphabet includes one event the diagram never draws, so a solution that
assumes every name it is handed is one of the six meets a counter-example
without the generator having to know which pairs are legal -- deciding that is
the reference solution's job, not this file's.
"""

EVENTS = ("submit", "reject", "approve", "revise", "publish", "archive",
          "frobnicate")


def generate(rng, count):
    return [_case(rng, index + 1) for index in range(count)]


def _case(rng, index):
    length = rng.randint(5, 10)
    events = [rng.choice(EVENTS) for _ in range(length)]
    return {
        "name": "random walk #%d" % index,
        "stdin": "".join(event + "\n" for event in events),
        "description": "A random sequence of events, legal and not. The "
                       "state after each one comes from the diagram.",
    }

tests.name: no events at all
tests.description: Nothing to print. The document is still in Draft, but nothing asked.

tests.name: the happy path
tests.description: Straight down the diagram, one arrow at a time.

tests.name: refused in Draft
tests.description: `approve` is an arrow out of Review, not out of Draft. The state has to stay where it was.

tests.name: rejected back to Draft
tests.description: The cycle in the diagram: a document can go round more than once.

tests.name: Archived is terminal
tests.stdin:
submit
approve
publish
archive
submit
revise
tests.expected_stdout:
Review
Approved
Published
Archived
REFUSED
REFUSED
tests.description: No arrow leaves Archived, so everything after it is refused.

tests.name: an event that is not on the diagram
tests.description: An unknown name is refused like any other pair the diagram does not draw -- not a crash, and it must not disturb the state.
